test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II ( JSO ) 2021 Official Paper ( Held On: 10 August 2022 )
subject: general
question: If the population skewness of the observations 8, 6, 3, 1, 2, 5 is 0.233, then the population skewness of 16, 12, 6, 2, 4, 10 is:
solution:
Skewness of a data set can be calculated using the formula:

S_k = frac{sum(x_i- bar{x})³}{sigma³}

where deviations deviations from the mean are calculated as (observation - mean). This formula takes into account the asymmetry of

the data set by considering the deviations raised to the power of 3, and then divided by the cube of the standard deviation to normalize the result.

Multiplying every value in the data set by a constant factor will result in the same skewness, as the mean, standard deviation, and

deviations from the mean will all be multiplied by the same constant factor.
